note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.” The children are the disciples, us, and Christ took part of the same flesh and blood. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham”, which is flesh and blood. “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” In all things, not some things. How is a man made like his brethren in all things? By having a father and a mother.

Then Hebrews 7: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.” He sprang out of Judah based on his father. The tribe comes from the father, as every Israelite’s does.

The fathers show the same. God told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels.” David knew “that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne.” And Paul says Christ “was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.” According to the flesh: made flesh and blood like his brethren.

That is why Matthew says “When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” Coming together was the customary wedding feast, as when Laban “made a feast” and Jacob went in unto his wife. Joseph and Mary were already espoused, and betrothal is marriage, so there was no fornication; they lay together before the feast. Child of the Holy Ghost means child of prophecy, the prophecy made to David. Joseph, a just man, was “not willing to make her a publick example”, which means stoned to death, and “was minded to put her away privily”: to hide her, because the child was his. Why would a just man hide a woman for something he did not do? And the angel called him “Joseph, thou son of David.” So our Lord sprang out of Judah through his father, made like his brethren in all things.

precepts.text: We see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come a little lower than the angels. It became him to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings: the captain of our salvation is the captain of the Lord's host that we read about with Joshua.
precepts.point: And he said, Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come. Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is talking about Christ.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
By Jericho, Joshua saw a man standing over against him “with his sword drawn in his hand”, and Joshua stepped to him: “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” You for me or for my enemies? Let me know. And he answered, “Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Who is the captain of the host of the Lord? This is talking about Christ, and Hebrews shows it.

“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.” He came down a little lower than the angels when he came the last time. Before that, in Exodus, he did not come a little lower than the angels; he came down like an angel. That is how he stood before Joshua with his sword drawn.

“For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect”. The captain of our salvation is the captain of the host of the Lord, the Lord of armies, that we read about with Joshua in Joshua 5. That was Christ who was there.

This is the book of the wars of the Lord. The same Christ who led the host when Israel came out of Egypt and conquered the land, and who is the captain of our salvation, is the one who fights for Israel. Joshua fell on his face and worshipped him, because the battle is the Lord's.

precepts.text: It became him, for whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory. That glory is a new body and a new mindset, so keep trying, keep working, do not give up over the little things you are going through.
precepts.point: As by one man's disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous. The first platform was broken by Adam; Christ did it right, so we build righteousness on him and reach the door through mercy, since our own righteousness is filthy rags. He did not come for the righteous, so brothers who talk down leadership as if they are already healed can be left alone.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
“For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.” By one man’s offence death came into the earth, from Abraham to Moses until today. The first platform we had, Adam messed up. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build righteousness upon him.

Hebrews shows where that obedience is leading: “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.” Christ’s death is going to bring many sons unto glory.

Do you know what that glory is? A new body and a new mindset. So while you are here on this earth, keep on trying. Keep on working. Do not give up and do not give in, no matter what. Keep on fighting. The little things you are going through, you are going to be all right.

The captain of our salvation was made perfect through sufferings, so our sufferings are not the end of the story. It is through mercy that we make it to the door, because our own righteousness is as filthy rags. Christ did not come for the righteous but for the sick, to heal them; the ones who talk down leadership as though they are healed already can be left alone. The rest of us keep building on the one who did it right.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.” The Father, “in bringing many sons unto glory”, made “the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.”

The captain of their salvation is Jesus Christ. The captain of the host of the Lord who told Joshua to loose his shoe is that captain, and he gave Joshua the very command given to Moses at the bush. Precept upon precept, the angel of the Lord in the burning bush was Christ.

precepts.text: He took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham, and in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.
precepts.point: Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
Christ was the angel in the bush, but he was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.”

“Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.” He was born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die. The God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Jacob who spoke out of the bush took on the seed of Abraham to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

precepts.text: We see Jesus, made perfect through sufferings, the captain of their salvation; Christ is the captain of the host.
precepts.point: The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“Nay; but as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Host means army: he is the captain, the leader, of the army of the Lord. And who is that captain? “But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour”, and it became him, in bringing many sons unto glory, “to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.”

The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. That is why Joshua, who had no fear walking up to a man with his sword drawn, fell on his face to the earth and did worship when he realized who stood before him, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant: “What saith my lord unto his servant?” Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is.

precepts.text: We see Jesus made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory, made the captain of our salvation perfect through sufferings.
precepts.point: Christ had to be made lower than the angels so that he could die. In his angelic form he would be immortal; he had to come after the seed of Abraham, David, and Joseph, from sperm, so that he could taste death for every Israelite man.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
David asks, “What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.” Paul tells us who that son of man is. He quotes David, “But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels”, and then names him: “But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.”

The so-called yaya israelites say the foolish thing that Jesus was an idol not prophesied in the Old Testament. But David is writing about a son of man made lower than the angels; that son of man is Jesus Christ, the black messiah.

Christ had to be made lower than the angels so that he could die. In his angelic form he would be immortal; he had to come after the seed of Abraham, David and Joseph, from sperm, so that he could taste death for every Israelite man. “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.” He is the captain of our salvation, made perfect through sufferings.

“For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.” The dominion David speaks of, all things under his feet, is Christ's, though we do not yet see it all.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
“For verily he took not on him the nature of angels;” For verily he took not on him immaculate conception. Don't keep going by that. The angels didn't come by sex; God just created them, like when he brought forth Christ in the beginning. He took not on him the nature of angels: Christ, when he came, didn't come the way the angels came, when God just created them like that. “but he took on him the seed of Abraham.” The seed of Abraham. Son of man.

“Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren,” Didn't we just read about his brothers in Matthew 13:55? He had four brothers, and he was made like them. So you mean his four brothers were immaculately conceived too? No. Son of man.

“that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.” How could he be a faithful high priest for us if he didn't go through what we went through, if he wasn't born like we were born? In order for him to be faithful and understand what we go through mentally, spiritually and physically, he had to be like us. He was made just like we were. Son of man.
